question: In which year did India's ‘National Food for Work Programme’ begin?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**2004**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **National Food for Work Programme** was launched in **November 2004**.
 
• This programme was introduced by the **Government of India** to address **poverty and unemployment** in rural areas.
 
• The scheme aimed to provide supplementary food security and employment opportunities to the **most disadvantaged sections of society**.
 
• It was implemented in **150 of the most backward districts** in the country.
 
• The programme provided **unskilled manual work** to individuals in exchange for food grains as wages.
 
• The funding for this scheme was entirely from the **Government of India**, making it a **centrally sponsored programme**.
 
• The initiative was eventually subsumed under the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) in 2006**, which expanded the scope of rural employment and development.
